rows.restated: This rule permits the assistant to automatically set the "priority" argument for the create_problem tool by looking at the provided "impact" and "urgency" values and using the specified mapping table; it disallows using any other inputs or a different method to determine priority, and it only applies when the create_problem tool is being called and a priority value is required.
rows.why: The rule correctly describes the mapping from impact and urgency to priority as given in the policy text, and restricts its application to the create_problem tool when priority is required, matching the table's intended use.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_problem tool to set the 'priority' argument, it may derive the priority value from the provided 'impact' and 'urgency' inputs according to the specified table. Any priority value not matching the table mapping for the given impact‑urgency pair is forbidden.
rows.why: The rule correctly captures the mapping from impact and urgency to priority as specified in the table, and forbids any deviation from that mapping.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool, it may set the priority argument only by deriving it from the provided impact and urgency values according to the specified mapping table; any other method of setting priority or using different inputs is not allowed.
rows.why: The rule accurately restates that priority must be derived solely from impact and urgency using the mapping table, matching the policy text's explicit mapping and implied restriction.

rows.restated: This rule permits the assistant to call the update_incident tool with the priority argument set to a value derived from the impact and urgency inputs according to the specified mapping table, and it forbids setting priority to any other value. It applies whenever the assistant has both impact and urgency values to determine the priority.
rows.why: The rule correctly captures the mapping from impact and urgency to priority as defined in the policy table, and forbids other values, matching the policy's intent.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the tool update_incident to change an incident’s status (identified by incident_id), it may only transition the status according to the defined edges: from 'new' to 'in_progress', 'on_hold', or 'resolved'; from 'in_progress' to 'on_hold' or 'resolved'; from 'on_hold' to 'in_progress'; and from 'resolved' to 'closed' or back to 'in_progress'. Any other status change is forbidden, and the rule applies specifically to calls that set the 'status' argument of update_incident.
rows.why: The rule accurately restates all allowed status transitions from the policy text, including the on_hold logging requirement, and correctly limits its scope to update_incident calls setting the status argument.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool and sets the "status" argument, it may only use one of the values "new", "in_progress", "on_hold", "resolved", or "closed"; any other status value is prohibited.
rows.why: The rule accurately restates the allowed status values from the policy text and applies the restriction to the correct tool and argument.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_incident tool, the status argument may only be set to one of the following values: new, in_progress, on_hold, resolved, or closed. Any other value for status is prohibited.
rows.why: The rule restates the exact same set of allowed status values as the policy text, with no additional restrictions or omissions.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool and supplies a resolution_code argument, only the values "fixed", "workaround", "not_reproducible", and "closed_by_caller" are permitted; any other value is disallowed. This rule applies specifically to the resolution_code parameter of the create_incident tool call.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the allowed values for the resolution_code parameter from the policy text, with no added or missing restrictions.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_incident tool and supplies a resolution_code argument, only the values "fixed", "workaround", "not_reproducible", or "closed_by_caller" are allowed; any other value is prohibited. This rule applies to every invocation of update_incident that includes a resolution_code parameter.
rows.why: The rule accurately restates the allowed values for resolution_code and applies to every update_incident call with that parameter, matching the policy text.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_change tool, the status argument is allowed only the values "new", "assess", "authorize", "scheduled", "implement", "review", "closed", or "canceled"; any other value is prohibited. This rule applies each time the create_change tool is invoked with a status parameter.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the allowed status values from the policy text and applies them to the create_change tool's status parameter without adding or omitting any values.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_change tool, the status argument may only be set to one of the following values: new, assess, authorize, scheduled, implement, review, closed, or canceled. Any other value for status is prohibited.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the allowed status values from the policy text without adding or omitting any.

rows.restated: When calling the tool link_new_incident_sla, the assistant may set the stage argument only to one of the following values: in_progress, paused, completed, cancelled, or breached. Any other value for stage is disallowed, and this restriction applies every time the link_new_incident_sla tool is invoked.
rows.why: The rule restates the allowed values for the stage argument exactly as listed in the policy text, with no additional restrictions or omissions.

rows.restated: When calling the tool update_incident_sla_details, the stage argument is allowed only the values in_progress, paused, completed, cancelled, or breached; any other value is prohibited. This restriction applies each time the update_incident_sla_details tool is used.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the allowed values for the stage argument from the policy text, applying the restriction to the update_incident_sla_details tool.

rows.restated: When calling the delete_incident_slas tool, the 'stage' argument is allowed only the values "in_progress", "paused", "completed", "cancelled", or "breached"; any other value for 'stage' is prohibited. This restriction applies each time the delete_incident_slas tool is used.
rows.why: The policy text only lists allowed values for 'incident_sla.stage' but does not mention the 'delete_incident_slas' tool or any tool-specific restriction. The rule incorrectly associates the restriction with a specific tool call.

rows.restated: When calling the create_incident tool, the status argument is allowed only the value "new"; any other status value is prohibited. This restriction applies to every use of the create_incident tool (source §3.1).
rows.why: The policy states all new incidents are set to status=new, which matches the rule's restriction that only 'new' is allowed when creating an incident.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_change tool with the argument "assigned_to", the field "active" must be set to "true" (any other value is not allowed). This rule applies to those calls and may be used to deny the request if the "active" field is not "true".
rows.why: The rule requires 'active' to be 'true' on the 'assigned_to' argument, but the policy requires the assigned user to be active, have Agent/Manager role, and be in the assignment group. The rule misses role and group membership constraints and applies 'active' to the wrong entity.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_change tool with the argument "assigned_to" and the field "role", only the values "Agent" or "Manager" are permitted; any other role value is disallowed and the request may be denied. This rule applies specifically to that tool‑argument‑field combination as defined in source §3.2.
rows.why: The rule incorrectly restricts the constraint to the create_change tool and a 'role' field, while the policy text applies to incident assignment generally and specifies that assigned_to must be an active user with the Agent or Manager role, not that a 'role' field must be one of those values.

rows.restated: When the create_change tool is invoked, the caller must be a member of the assignment_group that matches the assigned_to argument (as defined by source §3.2 and retyped from ID 96d374e7fa9b); the request can be denied if this membership condition is not met.
rows.why: The policy requires assigned_to to be an active user with Agent or Manager role and member of the assignment_group. The rule only requires the caller to be a member of the assignment_group, omitting the role and active status requirements.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_change tool with argument "assigned_to" and field "active", it may only set the value to "true"; any other value is prohibited and may be denied. This rule applies whenever that specific tool call is made, as defined by source §3.2.
rows.why: The rule references a non-existent 'update_change' tool and a field 'active', while the policy text concerns incident assignment constraints on 'assigned_to' and 'assignment_group'.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_change tool with the argument assigned_to, it may set the role field only to "Agent" or "Manager" (as specified in source §3.2). Any other role value is prohibited and may be denied.
rows.why: The rule references a tool (update_change) and a field (role) not mentioned in the policy text, which only specifies constraints on assigned_to and assignment_group.

rows.restated: This rule permits the assistant to call the update_change tool to modify the assigned_to field of a change record, but only when the caller is a member of the specified assignment_group (as defined by source §3.2). If the caller is not a member, the request may be denied.
rows.why: The rule adds a caller-membership condition not present in the policy text, which only requires the assigned_to user to be an active Agent/Manager in the group.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_problem tool and checks the 'assigned_to' argument, it may only proceed if the 'active' field of that argument is set to true; any other value can be denied. This rule applies specifically to reference_status checks for create_problem as defined in §3.2.
rows.why: The rule adds a condition about 'active' being true, which is not in the policy text, and omits the role and group membership requirements.

rows.restated: When the create_problem tool is used, the assigned_to argument’s role field may only be set to "Agent" or "Manager" (per §3.2); any other role is disallowed and can be denied.
rows.why: The rule restricts the role field on the assigned_to argument, but the policy text restricts the role of the user assigned, not a field on the argument.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_problem tool, it may allow the call only if the user specified in the assigned_to argument belongs to the group given in the assignment_group argument; if the user is not a member of that group, the call can be denied. This rule applies to every create_problem invocation that includes these two arguments.
rows.why: The rule restricts the create_problem tool, but the policy text does not mention any specific tool; it only states general incident assignment constraints.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_problem tool with the argument "assigned_to" and checks the "active" field, only the value "true" is allowed; any other value is prohibited and may be denied. This rule applies whenever that tool/argument/field combination is used, as specified in source §3.2.
rows.why: The rule references a specific tool (update_problem) and field (active) not mentioned in the policy text, which only states assignment constraints for assigned_to.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_problem tool and tries to set the assigned_to argument’s role field, it may only assign the role Agent or Manager; any other role is prohibited and can be denied. This rule is enforced for reference‑status checks under source §3.2 (retyped from 96d374e7fa9b).
rows.why: The rule incorrectly restricts the role field of the assigned_to argument, but the policy constrains the assigned_to user's role and group membership, not a field on the argument.

rows.restated: This rule permits the assistant to call the update_problem tool to modify the assigned_to field (using assignment_group as the group argument) when the source is §3.2, and it may deny the request. It forbids using update_problem for any other arguments or fields, and it only applies under the specified source and retyped‑from identifier.
rows.why: The rule references update_problem tool and source §3.2, which are not mentioned in the policy text; the policy only defines assignment constraints for assigned_to and assignment_group.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool, it may only proceed if the 'assigned_to' argument’s 'active' field is set to true; any other value is prohibited and can be denied. This rule applies specifically to reference‑status checks for the 'assigned_to' argument of create_incident (source §3.2).
rows.why: The rule only checks 'active' field, but the policy also requires 'Agent or Manager' role and membership in the specified assignment_group.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool, the assigned_to argument’s role field is only allowed to be ‘Agent’ or ‘Manager’; any other role may be denied. This rule applies to every create_incident tool call that includes an assigned_to argument.
rows.why: The rule only checks the role field, but the policy also requires the user to be active and a member of the specified assignment_group.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool, the value supplied for the assigned_to argument must belong to the group given in the assignment_group argument; if it does not, the call may be denied. This rule applies to every create_incident tool call.
rows.why: The rule requires assigned_to to belong to the assignment_group, but the policy only requires assigned_to to be an active user with Agent or Manager role and a member of the specified assignment_group. The rule omits the role and active status constraints, so it could deny calls the policy would allow.

rows.restated: When the assistant checks the reference status for the update_incident tool’s assigned_to argument, it may only proceed if the active field is set to true; any other value can be denied. This rule applies specifically to that tool‑argument combination and is enforced under source §3.2.
rows.why: The rule adds a condition about the active field being true, which is not mentioned in the policy text. The policy only requires assigned_to to be an active user with Agent or Manager role and membership in the assignment group.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_incident tool with the argument assigned_to, the role field must be either "Agent" or "Manager"; any other role is prohibited. This rule applies to every such tool call (per source §3.2) and may be used to deny the call if the role is not allowed.
rows.why: The rule only checks the role field, but the policy also requires the user to be a member of the specified assignment_group.

rows.restated: When the request comes from source §3.2 and references the ID 96d374e7fa9b, this rule lets members of the specified assignment_group update the incident's assigned_to field via the update_incident tool, and it can also deny that update; anyone not in that group (or not matching the source/ID) is not allowed to make the change.
rows.why: The rule adds conditions (source §3.2, ID 96d374e7fa9b, specific tool update_incident) not present in the policy text, which only states general assignment constraints without mentioning these restrictions.

rows.restated: When the incident status is "resolved", any call to the update_incident tool must include the arguments "resolution_code" and "resolution_notes"; the rule does not forbid the call and cannot be used to deny it.
rows.why: The rule correctly captures the requirement that resolution_code and resolution_notes must be provided when resolving an incident, and it does not add or omit any constraints from the policy text.

rows.restated: The rule permits using the create_change, update_change, and map_change_request tools only when a Change Request record is provided as the source of the change, enforcing that the Change Request field is required. It forbids creating or updating a change without linking it to a Change Request, and it applies whenever any of these three tools are invoked.
rows.why: The policy only requires changes to originate from a Change Request record. The rule adds specific tool names (create_change, update_change, map_change_request) and explicitly forbids creating or updating a change without linking it to a Change Request, which is a stronger restriction than the original text.

rows.restated: When calling the create_change tool, the status argument may only be set to "new"; any other value is prohibited. This rule applies to every invocation of the create_change tool.
rows.why: The policy says all new Changes are set to status=new, which matches the rule that only 'new' is allowed when creating a change.

rows.restated: When using the create_change or update_change tools, the change type must be one of the allowed enumeration values—standard, normal, or emergency. Any other change type is prohibited.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the allowed change types from the policy text and applies them to the specified tools without adding or omitting any values.

rows.restated: The assistant may call create_problem (and related problem/incident tools) only when a recurring incident pattern or a major incident has been identified; otherwise it must not create a problem. This rule applies whenever that trigger condition occurs.
rows.why: The rule accurately captures the trigger condition and the required action from the policy text, with no added restrictions or omissions.

rows.restated: When creating or updating a Problem or Incident, the assistant must verify that the Problem record links all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list, and must not allow the operation to proceed if that linking is missing.
rows.why: The policy only requires linking when a Problem record exists, but the rule also forbids creating or updating an Incident if the linking is missing, which the policy does not address.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_problem tool, it may set the status argument only to the value "new"; any other status value is prohibited. This restriction applies each time the create_problem tool is used.
rows.why: The rule correctly restricts the status argument to 'new' for the create_problem tool, matching the policy that all new Problems are set to status = new.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_problem tool and includes a workaround argument (any value), the status argument is allowed only the value "fix_in_progress"; any other status value is prohibited (the rule may be used to deny the call if this condition isn’t met).
rows.why: The rule restricts the status argument to 'fix_in_progress' when a workaround is provided during problem creation, but the policy text states that new problems default to status='new' and only set status='fix_in_progress' when a workaround is found, without linking this to the create_problem call. The rule incorrectly ties the workaround to the creation step and forbids other statuses that the policy allows at creation time.

rows.restated: The rule permits the assistant to call the update_problem tool with the status argument set to "fix_in_progress" only when a workaround argument is also provided (any value). In any other situation—different status values or no workaround—the call is disallowed.
rows.why: The rule only requires a workaround argument to set status to fix_in_progress, but the policy text also requires updating the workaround field and publishing workaround_notes to linked Incidents and Knowledge Articles. The rule misses these additional requirements.

rows.restated: For procedures (source 4.2), the rule permits using the incident and knowledge‑article tools—create/update incidents, create/update knowledge articles, and link or unlink knowledge articles to incidents—to ensure that any workaround notes are published to the associated incidents and relevant knowledge articles; it forbids leaving those notes unpublished.
rows.why: The rule restates the policy's requirement to publish workaround notes to linked incidents and relevant knowledge articles, using the specified tools, without adding or omitting any obligations.

rows.restated: The rule permits a Problem to be moved to the 'Closed' final status only when a permanent fix has been successfully applied through a linked normal or emergency Change Request. It forbids closing a Problem without such a linked Change Request, and it applies whenever a Problem's state transition to 'Closed' is attempted.
rows.why: The rule captures the same condition as the policy text: closing a Problem requires a permanent fix implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request. It does not add or omit any constraints.

rows.restated: The rule permits the system to automatically assign a priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) using the predefined Impact × Urgency matrix, and requires that any priority value be derived from that matrix; it forbids setting or changing priority by any other method. It applies whenever a priority is being determined or verified.
rows.why: The rule adds an explicit prohibition against setting or changing priority by any other method, which is not stated in the policy text.

rows.restated: When any of the listed change, problem, or incident tools are used, the assistant must verify that the IT asset is recorded in the configuration_item table; calls that do not include this required field are forbidden.
rows.why: The rule adds conditions (use of change, problem, or incident tools) not present in the policy text, which simply requires all IT assets to be recorded without tool-specific triggers.

rows.restated: When using the link_affected_ci_to_incident tool with a configuration_item argument, the rule permits the operation only if the CI’s status field is set to "in_use" or "maintenance"; any other status value is forbidden. This rule applies whenever the tool checks the configuration_item’s status, as defined in source §5.1.
rows.why: The rule correctly restricts linking to CIs with status 'in_use' or 'maintenance', matching the policy text exactly.

rows.restated: When the assistant tries to use the tool link_affected_ci_to_incident, it must not do so if the record’s status field is either retired or disposed. In all other status values the tool call is permitted.
rows.why: The rule correctly restates the policy: it forbids linking when status is retired or disposed, and permits it otherwise, matching the original text exactly.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the register_configuration_item tool, it must include the "owner_id" argument; if that argument is missing, the call may be denied. This requirement applies to every invocation of that tool.
rows.why: The rule correctly requires owner_id for every register_configuration_item call, matching the policy's requirement that all CIs must have a recorded owner_id.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the tool update_incident for an incident whose status is on_hold and whose on_hold_reason is Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem, it must also call the tool update_incident_sla_details if the incident’s stage is paused; calling update_incident under those conditions without the subsequent SLA‑details update is not allowed.
rows.why: The rule requires calling update_incident_sla_details only if the stage is already paused, but the policy requires pausing the SLA (setting stage to paused) when the incident is on_hold with the specified reasons, regardless of current stage.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the tool link_knowledge_to_incident, the argument used_as may only be set to one of the three values: suggested, applied, or resolution. Any other value for used_as is prohibited, and the rule applies only to calls of that specific tool.
rows.why: The rule correctly restricts the used_as argument to the three specified values for the link_knowledge_to_incident tool, matching the policy text exactly.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_incident tool with the argument assigned_to, the incident’s active field is allowed to be only "true"—any other value is forbidden. This rule applies to reference_status checks for that tool as specified in §8.1.
rows.why: The rule restricts the incident's active field, but the policy text restricts the user's active field.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the update_incident tool with a status of "closed", it must also call list_child_incidents for that incident, unless the condition "mandatory dependencies are satisfied" is true.
rows.why: The rule only applies to the update_incident tool and closing incidents, while the policy text applies to closing any record and verifying all mandatory dependencies, not just child incidents.

rows.restated: When the assistant calls the create_incident tool, it must include the arguments caller_id, short_description, impact, and urgency; calling the tool without all of these arguments is not allowed. This rule applies to every attempt to use the create_incident tool.
rows.why: The rule correctly requires the same four arguments as the policy text for the create_incident tool, and it does not add or omit any conditions.

rows.restated: Whenever the assistant calls the create_incident tool, it must also call the link_knowledge_to_incident tool with the parameter used_as set to "suggested"; creating an incident without that linked‑knowledge call is not allowed. This duty applies every time create_incident is used.
rows.why: The policy requires a search for relevant knowledge and linking matching articles when an incident is created, but does not mandate that the link_knowledge_to_incident tool be called every time create_incident is used—only when matching articles are found. The rule imposes an unconditional duty to call the tool, which is stricter than the policy.

rows.restated: For users with the manager role, any time they have been granted one of the listed actions (e.g., add_child_incident, create_incident, update_incident, etc.), they are forbidden from calling any of the specified tools (such as add_location, update_user_details, send_notification, etc.).
rows.why: The policy grants managers full CRUD and additional permissions, while the rule forbids them from calling specified tools, which contradicts the policy.

rows.restated: Agents are forbidden from calling any of the listed tools (e.g., add_location, add_new_user, send_notification, etc.) whenever they have any of the specified permissions such as add_child_incident, create_incident, update_incident, etc. The rule does not grant any permissions; it only imposes this restriction.
rows.why: The rule forbids calling listed tools when having certain permissions, but the policy text grants full CRUD on specific tables and only restricts bypassing approvals or changing system administration settings. The rule introduces unrelated restrictions not present in the policy.

rows.restated: Reporters who have the "update_incident" grant are forbidden from calling any of the listed tools (e.g., add_child_incident, create_incident, update_user_details, etc.). This restriction applies whenever a reporter possesses the "update_incident" permission.
rows.why: The rule introduces a permission ('update_incident') and lists specific tools not mentioned in the policy text, while the policy text describes general access to own incidents/requests and restrictions on others' records, CMDB, and internal notes.
